basis.eligible_universe: at least ten seasons carrying a WAR row, and a last season at least 5 years back
basis.jaws: the mean of career WAR and WAR7, which is the published definition

line.blocked_because: A Hall-sized line needs the count of players inducted AS PLAYERS, and no field in this data says what a plaque says. The source records the ELECTORATE that voted, and 147 inductees inside the eligible universe carry a route we cannot verify, among them Connie Mack, Casey Stengel, Joe Torre, John McGraw, Clark Griffith, Miller Huggins, Ned Hanlon and Bill McKechnie. A line sized on a Hall that counts them is not a player line. Excluding them does not fix it either: dropping a contributor from the ledger does not unlabel him, it makes him a resolved zero, and this page would then be publishing that Joe Torre is above the Hall line and not in the Hall of Fame.
line.by_class_blocked_because: position class misfiles every catcher who retired before roughly 1930. The catcher class holds 267 players in the eligible universe and 0 of them started before 1930, which is not a fact about catchers. 825 rows fall back to the positional-rate basis and 750 of those last played before 1953, when the fielding run components begin.

reproduction.what_it_means: this is a reproduction of a public shelf, not an improvement on it. The large disagreements sit in the Negro Leagues and pre-1901 population, where the two sources count different seasons.

coverage.why_a_blank_public_column_is_not_a_zero: a blank HoF Monitor or HoF Standards cell means the player never appeared on a Hall of Fame election page, so Baseball-Reference published no value for him. It does not mean zero.
coverage.war_ink_is_ours: WAR ink is ours and it is NOT Bill James's Black Ink or Gray Ink. It scores four points for a league-leading WAR season and one for a top-ten season, ranking hitters and pitchers in a single pool per league-season. Do not read it next to a published Black Ink number.
coverage.position_basis: position class is inferred from the fielding run components where they exist, which is 1953 and later, and from the positional adjustment rate before that. Every pre-1930 catcher on this page is misfiled, and the basis column says which method produced each row.
coverage.induction_column: inducted as a player by the writers is the only induction this page can verify from its own data. Every other route reads as route unverified, because the source records which electorate voted and not what the plaque says. That is why this page publishes no Hall line and no snub list.

watch.why_no_projection: this board ranks active players by what they have already done, against the same shelf as the retired board. A pace curve needs a per-age remaining-career WAR model, a backtest run forward on players who have already retired, and a year-filtered feature frame. None of those three exists yet, so this page does not guess.

not_yet_eligible.why: these players have ten or more seasons and last played in 2022, 2023 or 2024, so they have not cleared the five-year wait and are on neither the eligible board nor the active board.

bakeoff.label: bbwaa
bakeoff.headline: Baseball-Reference's Hall of Fame Monitor separates the Hall better than our WAR shelf does. Every one of our columns loses to it by more than the margin this sample can resolve, and the loss survives a multiplicity correction. That is the finding, and it is published because the point of this panel was to benchmark the shelf against the public work instead of asserting over it.
bakeoff.why_it_loses: HoF Monitor is built from batting titles, MVP shares, All-Star selections and postseason play. None of that is in our feature set, so this is a statement about missing data rather than about modelling.
bakeoff.population_note: this is NOT the eligible universe. It is almost exactly the set of players a screening committee already put on a Baseball-Reference ballot page, so an AUC here is discrimination among candidates that committee already advanced.

calibration.note: the same column also carries the lowest pooled Brier. The calibration-error leg resolves nothing at all; Brier and log loss resolve, and every resolved cell points the same way.

bakeoff.what_it_does_not_show: that our shelf is wrong. It reproduces the public WAR shelf almost exactly, which is what the leaderboard claims. It shows that WAR alone orders Hall of Fame outcomes less well than a rule that also counts awards and postseason play.

predictor.why: no induction probability is published until a merit model has passed its own gate against the best public baseline. The public baselines are already near the ceiling on this label, so the honest expected outcome is a tie.

franchises.why: the season frame carries no team column and there is no franchise continuity map in this repo. Beyond the map, crediting a multi-team career needs a frozen attribution rule with the rejected alternative named, which is a gate and not a query.

what_this_page_does_not_claim: that it knows who belongs in the Hall of Fame, that it knows what a plaque says, or that its WAR shelf is better than the public one it reproduces. Four of its eight sections are dark and each says what it is blocked on.
